description: Olive stalks tied off with cord, dry to the heart. Fodder, thatch, bedding — and the best tinder on the road.
lore: Ask three people what it is for and get fodder, thatch and bedding. Ask anyone who keeps a fire and get one answer. A twist of it rides inside the coat, against the body, where it stays dry through whatever the sky is doing; it comes out last, it goes under the kindling, and it is the difference between a lit hearth at dusk and a cold one.

There is a girl on one of the western rotas — one of the few [[lore/the_age_of_fires|still kept]] — who let hers get wet at a ford and walked four hours back for another twist rather than come in and say so. She was fourteen when she died. She has kept that fire ninety years and she is still fourteen, and the walk back is what the other keepers tell about her, in the tone people use for somebody they intend to be proud of forever.
gm_notes: Children keep rotas too, and keep them for centuries at the age they arrived. Use her sparingly; she is a whole quest if she ever needs to be.
